sourceKind: owner-export snapshot of already-public roadmap and backlog cards, owner-approved allowlist; source exports generated 2026-07-14 to 2026-11-10; not live

cards.title: Enable Account Portal to Fitness Handoff
cards.summary: Let people who begin in the Fawxzzy account portal continue straight into Fitness without a second sign-in step.

cards.title: Complete Self-Service Account Tools
cards.summary: Finish the self-service account lifecycle: recovering a forgotten sign-in, downloading your own data, and removing your account.

cards.title: Finish Account Site Setup for the Fitness App
cards.summary: Complete the shared account site that Fitness relies on for sign-in, sign-out, forgotten-sign-in recovery and returning people to the app, so the account side is finished before more Fitness work builds on it.

cards.title: Add Active User and Product Usage Statistics
cards.summary: Track enough usage to understand activation and retention.

cards.title: Make Sign-In Outcomes Clear
cards.summary: Show a clear message whenever a sign-in attempt does not complete, instead of quietly returning to the sign-in form.

cards.title: Build Curated Workout Engine V1
cards.summary: Create a simple guided program generator so users can get a routine without designing one manually.

cards.title: Expand Curated Workout Engine Beyond V1
cards.summary: Improve the workout engine with smarter recommendations after the V1 generator exists.

cards.title: Add Achievements and Badges
cards.summary: Add lightweight achievements after core retention loops exist.

cards.title: Expand Achievements and Earned Notifications
cards.summary: Plan a richer deterministic achievements phase and once-only earned notifications after the current achievement review is accepted.

cards.title: Ship Curated Onboarding Intake And Generator Handoff
cards.summary: Turn the dormant curated onboarding flow into a real first-time guided setup lane that captures training goal, experience, equipment, schedule, preferences, and constraints, persists the intake per member, and hands the bounded payload to the curated engine contract without pretending generation exists when it does not.

cards.title: Expand Earned Install Promotion Moments
cards.summary: Expand the earned install prompt beyond the first shipped post-workout moment so install asks happen after real product value and only on supported device paths. This should remain a capability-aware promotion lane, not a return to install-first gating.

cards.title: Harden Atlas Contracts and CI Environment Verification
cards.summary: Keep Fitness contract exports and environment verification deterministic across local and hosted CI.

cards.title: Return a Proper Not-Found Status for Missing Pages
cards.summary: Pages for items that do not exist or are unavailable should respond with a real not-found status along with the friendly not-found screen.

cards.title: Ship Shareable Workout Recap Artifacts
cards.summary: Generate one deterministic workout recap artifact from completed session truth so users can review, share, or export a clean summary without building a social feed. The artifact should highlight workout summary, PR moments, and consistency signals when grounded in real data.

cards.title: Make Workout Start Atomic
cards.summary: Make starting a workout an all-or-nothing step so an interrupted start never leaves a partial session behind.

cards.title: Add Calendar View
cards.summary: Give users a visual way to see training consistency over time.

cards.title: Add Workout Streaks
cards.summary: Add simple streak tracking to increase habit formation.

cards.title: Add Consistency Heatmap
cards.summary: Add GitHub-style workout consistency visualization.

cards.title: Add Weekly and Monthly Progress Summaries
cards.summary: Create periodic summaries that make progress feel real.

cards.title: Respect the Local Day Boundary in Workout Streaks
cards.summary: Count streak days in the user's local time zone so an evening workout is credited to the day it was logged.

cards.title: Add Optional Planned Workout Days
cards.summary: Distinguish optional workout days from required and rest days without weakening adherence, missed-day, or streak truth.

cards.title: Add Per-Exercise Exercise Timer System
cards.summary: Add a deterministic per-exercise timer system to session logging for exercises the user wants to time while they are actively performing them. The timer should be optional when an exercise is added, belong to the session exercise rather than the whole workout, appear during Current Session logging when enabled, and persist bounded timer outcomes for later analytics and history reuse.

cards.title: Add Exercise Timer Toggle When Adding an Exercise
cards.summary: Add a switch control in the add-exercise flow that enables or disables an exercise timer for that exercise in the current session. If enabled, the add flow should support a bounded timer configuration such as a target duration or timer mode. If disabled, the exercise should behave exactly like today with no timer UI added later in session logging.

cards.title: Show Live Per-Exercise Timer During Current Session Logging
cards.summary: When a timer-enabled exercise is open in Current Session, show the timer control in the logger surface for that exercise. The user should be able to start, pause, resume, reset, or dismiss the timer while performing the exercise without affecting the saved set truth. If a target duration exists, completion should surface a clear done-state cue for that exercise.

cards.title: Persist Exercise Timer Outcomes Into Session Analytics
cards.summary: Persist exercise-timer configuration and usable outcome data into session truth. At minimum, store whether the exercise used a timer, the configured timer target or mode when present, and enough completed timing data to support later summaries and comparisons. This must survive session completion and be available to history-family loaders without reconstructing timer behavior from fragile client-only state.

cards.title: Add Separate Recovery And Rest Recommendation Layer
cards.summary: Add a separate backend and product lane for recovery summaries, rest recommendations, and next-set prompts. This may use set timestamps, session history, and any later bounded timing truth, but it must remain a separate concern from the toggleable exercise timer feature. The app can later surface deterministic guidance such as likely rest windows or recovery patterns without redefining the user-facing exercise timer as a rest timer.

cards.title: Show Live Active User Presence on Today
cards.summary: Show a privacy-preserving aggregate active-user count on Today without exposing individual identities.

cards.title: Maintain the mobile-clean 2D shipping baseline
cards.summary: Keep the current Phaser maze readable, responsive, mechanically faithful, and regression-safe across supported desktop and mobile play.

cards.title: Adopt the shared account consumer contract
cards.summary: Use the canonical public-client authorization flow and shared account routes, keeping sensitive values out of the client and avoiding competing account screens.

cards.title: Harden sign-in: shared portal, refresh handling and retired-target rejection
cards.summary: Mazer replaced its own sign-in UI with the shared account portal (PR #350), restored the signed-out boot gate (PR #361), rejected retired provider targets (PR #364), fixed refresh and transient-failure handling (PR #370) and paused the menu AI until account access resolves (PR #369). Merged to main; live end-to-end acceptance is tracked separately.

cards.title: Finish the atomic sign-up username flow (blocked on provider)
cards.summary: Sign-up should claim the chosen username in the same step as account creation. The server-side contract merged (PR #280), but the client consumer in PR #281 is still open, conflicts with main and must not ship until the matching provider-side hook is confirmed live and proven. It has been open since 2026-08-25.

cards.title: Prove installed-app sign-in and progress end to end
cards.summary: Code fixes for retired-target rejection, AI progression hydration, menu-AI pause, session refresh and callback-error visibility are merged (PR #364, #367, #368, #369, #370). No end-to-end acceptance run exists yet: installed-app proof, natural session refresh, account recovery, cross-user isolation, authenticated progress hydration and whether the account handoff keeps an installed app standalone. It needs a real phone and a throwaway test account.

cards.title: Harden progress reset across devices with a reset epoch
cards.summary: Reset progress works server-first for one device, but a second device holding higher local progress would show the old level after a merge. The complete fix adds a reset counter on the server and makes both merge paths discard local data when it advances, which needs an approved database change. It has been held since 2026-11-06; version one may accept the residual risk. The owner delegated judgement calls on 2026-11-10 but a database change still needs explicit approval.

cards.title: Persist settings per account
cards.summary: Game settings are stored per signed-in account, with a remote profile row for sync. Delivered at source level per the storage doc.

cards.title: Finish the configurable AI runner and run-corpus calibration
cards.summary: The previous project board tracked an AI runner that a human can configure, plus a corpus of recorded runs used to calibrate run quality. The runner is nearly done and a first corpus packet exists on main. Remaining gap: calibration is unfinished, and any remote retention of runs would need a provider-side step.

cards.title: Add AI-assisted maze completion with spendable hints
cards.summary: The board wanted a way for a player to spend an allowance to have AI help finish a maze. Not started; depends on the economy contract.

cards.title: Decide whether the game has sound
cards.summary: There is no audio anywhere in the game and no sound setting. The audit proposes small synthesized effects unlocked on the first tap, with a Settings toggle. The owner must say if sound is allowed and whether it defaults on or off. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Compose and wire original Mazer music from the music-language brief
cards.summary: A research pass defined an original music language: restrained, weather-touched and ancient, with small modal motifs, and explicitly no lifted melodies from existing game scores. It recommends prototyping one title sting, one ambient loop and one storm cue first. Nothing is wired at runtime, and wiring waits until the shell audio setting is deliberately re-enabled.

cards.title: Align production auth persistence verification
cards.summary: Verify the current signed-out account gate and diagnostics-only authenticated setting persistence without touching real accounts or data.

cards.title: Add a play camera zoom and minimap (deferred)
cards.summary: The board asked for a play camera zoom with a minimap. The owner deferred the zoom lever; a zoom option normaliser existed at base, and the Board Zoom setting was later removed because board size is frozen. No minimap exists.

cards.title: Add shared-seed daily and weekly challenges
cards.summary: Daily and weekly challenges from a shared seed. Not started; server seed and leaderboard parts would be provider-gated, and the design needs an owner decision.

cards.title: Add a haptics setting and test the vibration helper
cards.summary: Vibration is one hard-coded pattern with no setting, no reduced-motion gating and no test; iOS support is unverified. Plan: a Settings toggle and a pin test.

cards.title: Make controls fluid and input movement correct
cards.summary: Two board cards covered fluid controls and motion, and correct player input and movement. Directional-intent and movement-pace contracts and active-play packets exist on main. Source-level verdict only.

cards.title: Retain Cyberdeck research as planning evidence
cards.summary: Deferred: keep the merged research synthesis available as planning evidence without claiming primary Cyberdeck implementation is active or approved.

cards.title: Complete the Supabase master cutover
cards.summary: Move Mazer production to the master project while preserving progression, identities, receipts, and the encrypted legacy recovery archive.

cards.title: Decide whether to raise the server-side difficulty cap and rank steps
cards.summary: The server keeps its own copy of the older difficulty ladder (a fixed cap and fixed rank thresholds), and the client ladder to level 198 deliberately stays inside it so no database change was needed. Raising the cap, changing the rank steps or adding a new ruleset needs an approved database change and is on hold.

cards.title: Finish the remote run receipt and playbook sync bridge
cards.summary: Remote receipts go through the completion outbox. The ATLAS and playbook sync parts still need provider or ATLAS steps with explicit owner approval.

cards.title: Finish the offline-first play, sync and conflict contract
cards.summary: A completion outbox and monotonic merge exist on main. The proposal for coins, inventory and checkpoint hierarchy is unsigned, and server parts are provider-gated.

cards.title: Land the multi-target deployment architecture doc
cards.summary: A long architecture note describes running Mazer as a browser game, an installable app and a dedicated hardware display target, with proof gates for each. It exists only as an untracked document in an old checkout and was saved as a patch, not committed. The owner needs to approve a docs-only PR with the stale status text refreshed.

cards.title: Sign the shop and random item economy contract
cards.summary: A draft contract for the coins, shop and random items is written but unsigned. Awaiting the owner sign-off; most NOT-STARTED cards depend on it.

cards.title: Add coin pickups, inventory and a data-driven cosmetic catalog
cards.summary: Three board cards cover maze coin pickups as cosmetic currency, an inventory with cosmetic unlocks, and a data-driven theme catalog. No code exists for coins or inventory at base. Awaiting the economy contract decision.

cards.title: Define account entitlements and store checkout
cards.summary: A draft entitlement contract exists, unsigned, and no entitlement objects exist in source. Store checkout is blocked on that contract plus provider and policy decisions; no checkout library is installed.

cards.title: Teach the controls and the goal on level 1
cards.summary: Nothing teaches movement today: the only legend is in a collapsed Guide inside Settings, and the touch stick appears only while touching. A tutorial module exists in source but no app code imports it, and level 1 is now a straight corridor so its content needs refreshing. Plan: a non-blocking ghost stick and one line (drag anywhere, or arrow keys) that fades on the first move, reusing the tutorial store.

cards.title: Add a level-complete moment
cards.summary: Clearing a level shows only a bare digit and lasers; there is no text, score or sound. Plan: inside the existing 2.6 s cadence, show Level N with a small CLEARED line, a halo burst and haptic, with a reduced-motion form. Not started.

cards.title: Add a rank-up moment
cards.summary: Rank changes silently at levels 6, 11, 17, 23 and 31. Plan: a tier-colored ring and letter for about 700 ms with a short sound and haptic, skippable. Depends on the chip decision and the level-complete beat.

cards.title: Decide whether to show a Level/Rank chip
cards.summary: Level and rank are invisible everywhere in play and menu, and the earlier no-score-panel stance blocks fixing it. The audit proposes a compact chip beside the pause control and a single vocabulary: Level, Rank (letter), Place (#N). It waits on the owner lifting that stance. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Confirm before quitting a level
cards.summary: Quit to Menu has no confirmation and is styled like a neutral action, so a mid-level attempt is discarded with one tap. Plan: a leave-this-maze confirmation after the first move using the existing confirm dialog.

cards.title: Decide: resume the same maze after quit or reload
cards.summary: Today quitting or reloading discards the attempt and the next Start rolls a new maze, which is a free re-roll for a stuck player. The proposal persists the maze seed so the same maze resumes, which needs seed plumbing. The owner has not chosen. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Decide what the menu demo maze shows
cards.summary: The menu demo follows the player's own track, so a new player sees the same corridor seven times while a level-40 player sees their own maze as wallpaper. Options: an independent attract loop or keep it. The audit notes the label split between player and AI skill is diagnostics-only. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Handle orientation flips mid-run
cards.summary: Rotating mid-run keeps the same maze, so the portrait corridor becomes about 8 px wide in landscape. Plan: auto-pause and refit, with a rotate-back prompt only if the corridor falls under 24 px, regenerating only at the next level.

cards.title: Flush the completion queue when back online and say so
cards.summary: Offline completions are queued and retried only at boot and on the next completion, with no online listener and no player-visible notice. Plan: an online listener and a once-per-outage notice that progress is saved.

cards.title: Polish the install gate copy and feedback
cards.summary: The install gate blocks every browser tab by design but gives a generic title, no value line, and no feedback after Copy link or a dismissed prompt. Plan: a short value line, a Link copied confirmation and a mini-maze graphic.

cards.title: Decide when input unlocks during the level intro
cards.summary: After a goal, input is locked about 2.5 s while the player marker is visible from 0.5 s. Unlocking earlier would speed play but touches timer, progression pacing and AI scoring, so it needs a product call. The owner also complained twice that build and deconstruct felt too fast, so pacing is sensitive. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Auto-pause when the page is hidden and fix lifecycle timing
cards.summary: A flow audit found that leaving the page did not pause a live run and that hidden time counted as run time. PR #392 opens Pause on hidden, page-hide and blur, excludes hidden time from the run timer and holds the intro and outro, and unblocks keyboard resume from the goal hold. Merged and deployed; real-device backgrounding is not yet verified.

cards.title: Smooth maze generation, reveal and menu-demo pacing
cards.summary: Players saw freezes and unsynced beams around goal reach. A series of PRs precomputed the next maze during a hold, synced the delivery beam to the build, fixed reveal order and corrected menu-demo state carry-over across mode switches, including PRs #298, #302, #307, #310, #315, #316 and #317. Merged to main.

cards.title: Deliver edge-wrap topology and notch fill
cards.summary: Edge-wrap topology diagnostics, a contract and an architecture test exist on main. The board card is complete at source level; no deployed or device claim is made.

cards.title: Extract the maze pattern engine and batch generator as contracts
cards.summary: Deferred: Two maze modules, the pattern engine and the batch generator, were documented as extraction candidates with inputs, outputs and lifecycle rules. Both still depend on the oversized shared maze core. The doc's own readiness verdict is refactor first: give each a dedicated source boundary and contract tests before promoting either.

cards.title: Fade wrap corridors out between levels 100 and 140 and price them
cards.summary: Wrap corridors used to switch off at level 120 and make level 120 about 88 steps longer than level 119. PR #404 fades them out from level 100 to 140 and prices each wrap's saving the way loops are priced, so a wrap cannot make a level easier than its target. The largest smoothed single-level step in levels 100 to 150 dropped from 19.4 times the median step to 2.3 times. It is merged and deployed on 2026-11-10. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and no wrap level was checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Keep the in-app Guide in sync with game and UI changes
cards.summary: Standing owner rule: any PR that changes controls, tiles, markers, wrap, levels or settings rows must update the Guide and its icons in the same PR, enforced by a drift test and a PR template checklist item.

cards.title: Govern the UI rework as single-owner integrator waves with a decision registry
cards.summary: The UI redesign is split into dependency-ordered waves, and a decision registry plus an architecture test allow only one active wave to own a shared UI path at a time. A change set that spans two waves fails a guard, so redesign work lands in small, separately reviewable pull requests. Completed waves hand paths off explicitly.

cards.title: Add the Mazer owner project-board export
cards.summary: A governance export of the Mazer project board for the owner, merged in PR #360 on 2026-10-13. This board refresh builds on it.

cards.title: Retire the previous project board and refresh this one from all prior discussion
cards.summary: The earlier Mazer board lived on a system that is now archived; its 66 cards were reconciled against the repository but never synced here. On 2026-11-10 the owner asked for this board to be filled from every earlier chat and project note, with completed work as history. The cards come from the tracker, audit ledger, reconciliation, chat closeouts and merged pull requests, and the public site still needs both refresh pull requests merged.

cards.title: Keep the visual proof discipline current
cards.summary: The board tracked the practice of proving visual changes with captured evidence. It is near complete; the rule is ongoing governance.

cards.title: Land the hazard foundations as dormant source
cards.summary: The hazard graph and solvability validator, hazard placement and loadout, practice bots, and a chaser and interceptor engine with a joint solver were merged in PR #373. They are switched off by design and no scene imports them. One chaser solves fine; two or more hit the solver cap and are treated as unsolved.

cards.title: Sign or reject the endless hazard product contract
cards.summary: A draft contract describes how obstacles, enemies and items enter the endless ladder in phases. It is unsigned, and five board cards (difficulty shaping, obstacles, enemies, items, cloak) are covered by it rather than standing alone. Awaiting the owner sign-off.

cards.title: Phase 2: introduce obstacles and enemies one at a time
cards.summary: Deferred: The owner wants difficulty to come from obstacles and enemies rather than from zooming or shrinking the board, but only after Phase 1 (visuals, progression, animation sync and game flow) is finished. Each hazard type is to be introduced alone, then developed, then combined, folded into the level ladder. The hazard layer stays dormant until the product contract is signed.

cards.title: Add obstacles, traps and puzzles (covered by the hazard phases)
cards.summary: The board card for an obstacle, trap and puzzle environment contract is covered by the obstacle phase of the hazard contract. The trap library on main is not live. Deferred until the hazard contract is signed.

cards.title: Make the pursuing enemy playable (covered by the hazard phases)
cards.summary: The board card for an enemy that pursues the player is now handled by hazard phases rather than as a standalone card. A graph-based enemy agent exists in the core library but no scene imports it, so it is a design reference, not a playable feature. Deferred to the hazard contract.

cards.title: Add usable items and the invisibility cloak (covered by the hazard phases)
cards.summary: Deferred: The board listed a mystery-box usable item system and an invisibility cloak. Both are folded into the item phase of the hazard contract; the item library is not live in any scene. Cloak scope is an owner decision.

cards.title: Complete the turn-synchronous world simulation beyond the player phase
cards.summary: A world turn host and contract exist on main with tests, and the board marked the card completed. In truth only the host and player movement phase are done; enemy, projectile, item, duration and collision handlers are intentionally unintegrated. Status kept honest as in progress.

cards.title: Plan hazard introduction and contact moments
cards.summary: When hazards land, each new type needs a skippable pre-level card and telegraph, and contact needs a one-time message, a flash and a pushback with brief invulnerability. This is phase 2 and depends on the unsigned hazard contract.

cards.title: Establish one deterministic app-icon authority
cards.summary: Generate every browser, Apple, PWA, maskable, Workbox, and shortcut icon from one exact master artwork.

cards.title: Land the MazeV2 convergence analysis contract
cards.summary: Provide deterministic canonical maze comparison, adapter, corpus, timeout, provenance, and nullable metric semantics.

cards.title: Build the moving procedural maze mode (deferred)
cards.summary: Four board cards covered a moving maze mode: the mode itself, lane correction, one-tile lane snap and assisted-motion proof. No moving-maze code exists and the owner deferred the whole set; they are merged here as one deliverable.

cards.title: Plan multiplayer and endless survival mode (deferred)
cards.summary: Two board cards covered a multiplayer foundation and an endless multiplayer survival mode. Neither is started; the owner deferred both and they are merged into one card.

cards.title: Adopt one motion scale for durations, loops and easing
cards.summary: The game has about 18 unrelated loop periods, 6 easings and 30 durations, and dead motion definitions that drive nothing. Proposal: a pure motion module with a 120/200/320/480/720 ms ladder, loops as harmonics of 1200 ms and one reduced-motion crossfade. Values were added to the theme in PR #381; consuming them in the scene is not started.

cards.title: Animate overlays, controls and the Start and splash transitions
cards.summary: Overlay open and close, hover, press, toggles and toasts are instant while maze transitions get eased motion, and pressing Start removes the title, icons and corridor in one frame while the HTML splash hard-cuts to the game. The plan is a 200 ms panel rise with staggered rows, 120 ms state changes, a short exit of menu chrome and a splash fade with a shared loader period. Not started.

cards.title: Fix step glide overlap and add wall-bump feedback
cards.summary: The player glide floor (90 ms) can exceed the repeat interval at max speed or with the touch stick, so held movement pulses; and a blocked move gives no visual or haptic feedback. Plan: derive glide from repeat with a stick cap, and add a 2 px nudge plus a light buzz.

cards.title: Add an in-game reduced-motion setting and finish the gating
cards.summary: Reduced motion follows only the OS setting; under it the title freezes mid-phase while the START color cycle and button blinks keep running. Plan: gate those animations, set a defined static alpha, add a persisted toggle in Settings and use one crossfade length.

cards.title: Plan the native app-store wrapper after web stabilization
cards.summary: Prepare a Capacitor-based native wrapper only after the web gameplay and UI baseline is stable and independently verified.

cards.title: Freeze Navigation Core v1
cards.summary: Ship the accepted floor, player, goal, and continuous trail rendering baseline with deterministic visual and lifecycle proof.

cards.title: Define a diagonal path graph contract (deferred)
cards.summary: The board held a card for allowing diagonal movement in the path graph, barely started. The owner deferred it.

cards.title: Cut the cold-boot payload from about 5.7 MB to about 1.6 MB
cards.summary: Cold boot preloaded several large images that nothing drew. PR #391 deleted them and shipped lossless HUD icons, and PR #375 retired unused diamond and teleport-beam art. A budget test now pins the preload list and byte sizes. The icon set precache and HUD texture size are still open follow-ups.

cards.title: Reduce canvas redraw cost and soften the throttle floor
cards.summary: Canvas replay of thousands of star and tile drawing commands costs 2.6-4.9 ms per frame even on a static overlay, and the frame governor drops ambient motion to 4 fps when frames average over 19 ms. Plan: bake the backdrop, stop forcing redraws, and floor the throttle at about 15 fps. Needs a real-device trace.

cards.title: Research a rotating planet maze
cards.summary: Deferred: retain the parked planet-maze research sequence without presenting it as current product work.

cards.title: Make level 1 a straight corridor
cards.summary: Level 1 became a straight corridor along the longer board axis, a difficulty change that the integration record flags as needing the owner sign-off. Merged in integration 1 (PR #373).

cards.title: Replace the difficulty ladder with a felt-difficulty ladder to level 198
cards.summary: Level 1 is the straight corridor and levels 2 to 198 take their geometry from one strictly rising target on a fixed board, measured by a deterministic goal-seeking explorer, with longer routes and deep deceptive branches and no zoom or size lever. The ladder (PR #395, replacing the draft in PR #385) merged on 2026-11-06 and was reported deployed on 2026-11-09. Felt difficulty is modelled, not player-tested, and the owner's difficulty sign-off is not recorded.

cards.title: Make maze geometry follow the displayed level
cards.summary: The owner saw a level label near 18000 on a maze that read like level 20 to 30. Geometry level came from a bounded stored target, so a high ordinal with a low target kept easy geometry. PR #400 makes geometry follow the displayed level and merged on 2026-11-10; deployment is not confirmed.

cards.title: Add shortcuts, alternate routes and decoy loops plus progression gauges
cards.summary: The owner asked for occasional shortcuts or multiple routes (sometimes only one way, perhaps scaling with maze size) and for ways to gauge progression scaling. PR #401 adds three loop kinds that keep the long route, priced felt difficulty and a gauge suite (shortest route, walker steps, random solver, human-like explorer), with level 1 staying a straight corridor. Merged on 2026-11-10; deployment and a real-phone check are not confirmed.

cards.title: Decide what happens past level 198 so levels keep getting harder
cards.summary: The felt-difficulty ladder rises strictly through level 198 on a fixed board with no zoom or size lever. Measured 2026-11-10: the explorer number cannot rise further because the board is at its 50 percent floor limit, so MAZER-PROG-013 (review) extends the ladder to level 268 with zero-felt-cost side stubs and declares the plateau there. What stays open is the lever after level 268: sign the hazard contract (MAZER-HAZ-002, hazardBudgetLevels starts at 268) or, only if hazards are rejected, a bigger board past a level, which is the zoom lever the owner ruled out. The owner wants levels to keep getting harder forever, so this decision cannot be settled by generation alone.

cards.title: Decide a minimum tile size for very large boards
cards.summary: On a 390 phone at level 99 the tile is about 6.5 px, so the player and goal are tiny whatever the tile style; the Chip bake also costs 58-69 ms on the largest boards. Needs a product call on minimum tile size or zoom, which the owner deferred. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Add milestone moments for levels past rank S
cards.summary: Deferred: From level 31 rank stays S, so nothing marks progress. Plan: every fifth level shows the level and a hazard-tier pip with a short chime. Depends on the ladder and hazard work.

cards.title: Decide which maze features unlock at which level and content band
cards.summary: Two board cards cover feature gating by level and a versioned manifest of content bands. Nothing is implemented; both depend on the ladder and budget decision and on the economy draft. Awaiting an owner decision.

cards.title: Preserve authoritative progression and fix level/target desync
cards.summary: Several fixes keep a player progress safe: monotonic completion replay (PR #282), authoritative historical hydration (PR #293), a production fix for level versus target complexity desync (PR #308), wider seed storage (PR #311) and AI hydration after the master consolidation (PR #368). Merged to main.

cards.title: Make board scale ceiling and feeder count device-relative
cards.summary: Difficulty-driven board scale and feeder count were raised and then made relative to the device so phones and desktop scale sensibly. PRs #301 and #304. Board size is now frozen again for the ladder, so no zoom lever is planned.

cards.title: Ship the perpetual play loop
cards.summary: Play mode loops from level to level without returning to a dead end. A packet and a lifecycle test referencing the loop exist on main (verified by reading).

cards.title: Show rank-only progression to the player
cards.summary: The progression display shows rank only, as recorded in the current-truth document. Delivered at source level.

cards.title: Extend the ladder to level 268 with side stubs the explorer does not pay for
cards.summary: The owner saw that the menu maze for level 18000 looks like a level 30 maze. Every level from 198 was the same maze class because the ladder steers on one explorer number and the board is full at level 198. Shrinking the route to raise that number made the other walkers 40 to 57 percent easier, so it was rejected. The new pull request adds exactly one more cell of short side stubs per level (the explorer does not enter stubs of 3 cells or fewer), which keeps the explorer number fixed and strictly orders levels 199 to 268 by cell count. At level 268 against 198 the maze has 38 route junctions instead of 12, 87 dead ends instead of 27 and the random walk takes 3.6 times as many steps. Levels 1 to 198 are byte-identical and levels 268 and above are one class again; the hazard hand-off now starts at 268. This is an open pull request, not merged and not deployed. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and the stubs are visible at a glance to a person.

cards.title: Harden PWA installability and delivery assets
cards.summary: Keep manifest, service-worker, icon, and install guidance truthful and reproducible without stale localhost service workers.

cards.title: Add PWA screenshots, iOS launch art and icon cleanup
cards.summary: The manifest has no screenshots, there is no iOS launch splash, the favicon is 221 KB, the manifest description is internal jargon, and the any-purpose icon shows baked black corners. Fix these plus the off-brand emblem. Large launch art files are frozen by provenance rules, so some need owner OK.

cards.title: Make the install gate deterministic and bound the account bootstrap
cards.summary: The install gate never appeared in a normal browser tab and sign-in could leave a blank page. PR #372 blocks every non-installed visit (with listed exemptions), adds a static boot splash and bounds account startup; PR #367 keeps OAuth callback errors visible past the gate. Merged to main.

cards.title: Settle the install gate policy and prove the offline shell
cards.summary: The manifest, offline shell, lifecycle handling and the install gate (PR #372) exist. Open points: the boot-time install gate blocks boot in some install modes without a skip, which clashes with the plan that access is enforced by entitlement, and offline reload after a warm install has no real-device proof.

cards.title: Verify deployed Mazer changes on a real phone and installed app
cards.summary: Everything shipped since 2026-11-06 was checked against bundles, tests and harness frames only. Real phone frame rate, touch feel, pixel density, iOS home-screen behaviour, hardware back, real backgrounding and felt difficulty at levels 60, 100 and 190 remain unchecked. The owner has not reported a phone pass in the late transcript.

cards.title: Close the mobile shell device harness with real-device proof
cards.summary: The harness exists but closure needs real-device proof, which has not happened.

cards.title: Keep the UI-surface capture and verification harness green
cards.summary: Harness repairs and verifiers: ui-surfaces capture restored (PR #362), stale label expectation fixed (PR #363), CI pinned to a supported Linux image (PR #371), render and visual tests added to the main test run (PR #380), Settings sheet capture and stale tests fixed (PR #389), and a harmless font-preload console hint ignored (PR #397). Merged to main; tooling only.

cards.title: Add a hidden Level Preview route for dev and QA
cards.summary: A hidden route starts play at a chosen level on the real generation path and real board without touching a real account: sandbox storage, no remote calls, a preview tag and a pause section to jump levels. Merged in PR #398 and kept out of the in-app Guide.

cards.title: Build a 1-500 level progression gallery for review
cards.summary: A capture tool renders one sample per level for levels 1 to 500 in parallel so difficulty progression can be reviewed visually. Built across PRs #290, #296, #299 and #300 with a rebuild document. Merged to main.

cards.title: Finish cross-viewport UI reliability and layout persistence
cards.summary: Two board cards cover UI reliability across viewports and browser layout persistence; packets from July exist. Both are partly done and remain open.

cards.title: Score run quality and store it on local receipts
cards.summary: The run quality metric contract v2 scorer, its test and local telemetry fields exist on main, although the board still showed them open at 0 percent. This is local only; remote versioned capture is not included.

cards.title: Show run quality to the player after a run (deferred)
cards.summary: A player-facing results display for run quality was deferred by the owner.

cards.title: Decide how run quality gates leaderboard and achievement entries
cards.summary: Two board cards cover admitting runs to the leaderboard and to achievements by quality. Leaderboard authority is server-side, so a change is provider-gated; the achievement rule is an owner decision. Neither started.

cards.title: Build the shared run status panel
cards.summary: A panel showing run status across surfaces was started and is early.

cards.title: Finish web share metadata, the preview image and external verification
cards.summary: Canonical and share tags exist and are pinned by a test, but the preview image is still the app icon and a dedicated preview asset is not confirmed. Verifying the preview on external platforms needs a deployed URL and checks outside the repository, so that part is gated.

cards.title: Define social profiles, friends and events (deferred)
cards.summary: The board had a contract card for social profiles, friends and events. Not started; deferred by the owner.

cards.title: Freeze Teleport System v1
cards.summary: Ship the single-primary gameplay transfer contract with pause-safe timing, deterministic anchor selection, and real lifecycle verification.

cards.title: Define a handcrafted asset authoring and import workflow
cards.summary: The board wanted a workflow for authoring and importing handcrafted art assets. Not started and awaiting an owner decision.

cards.title: Unify Settings into one sheet for menu and pause
cards.summary: The owner decided the in-game Settings layout is canonical and the main-menu Settings must match it fully, with the same structure. A shared Settings sheet now serves both menu and pause (PR #383 planned it, PR #386 wired it), and PR #390 removed the Close pill in favor of Back to Menu on the menu version and reclaimed the space. Checked on capture frames; not yet seen on a real phone.

cards.title: Add a server-first Reset progress action to Settings
cards.summary: The owner asked for a Reset progress button in the main-menu Settings that clears full account maze progression only, not the account or profile. PR #386 resets the server first and then local data, and the leaderboard level drops back to 1. The signed-in server reset has not been verified against the live database.

cards.title: Redo the in-app Guide as a shared sheet with matching icons
cards.summary: The owner asked to redo the Guide in both menu Settings and in-game Settings so it reflects the new look. A data-driven Guide sheet with icons drawn by the same functions as the board landed with the shared Settings sheet (PR #383, PR #386), and a drift test pins its claims to live game constants. It is kept current by the standing guide-sync rule.

cards.title: Redo the Leaderboard as a Settings-style sheet
cards.summary: The owner asked for the leaderboard to be redone entirely while keeping its icon. A first redesign shipped with the header and pause integration (PR #376), and PR #396 rebuilt it as a Settings-style sheet with a Back to Menu row, a pinned You row and seven states. Real leaderboard data on a phone has not been checked, and whether the column is called Rank or Place is an open naming call.

cards.title: Remove the Board Zoom setting
cards.summary: Board Zoom was a difficulty and framing lever the owner wanted kept out of play until obstacles and enemies are right. PR #396 removed it from Settings together with the leaderboard redesign, and the stored zoom value is scrubbed. Camera zoom stays deferred.

cards.title: Redo the Pause menu and remove the profile icon from it
cards.summary: The owner asked to redo the whole pause menu while keeping its icon and to remove the profile icon from it. The pause card is now Resume, Settings (collapsed) and Quit to Menu, and the profile icon is gone from Pause and Options (PR #376). Quit has no confirmation yet.

cards.title: Show the username beside the profile icon and drop the bottom Welcome line
cards.summary: The owner asked to remove the Welcome line and username at the bottom and show the username at the top left beside the profile icon, with no text background and some padding from the screen edge. This shipped in PR #376, with header edge padding in PR #382 and a clean label in PR #384. A CI check for the 320px label had to be loosened, and the label has not been seen on a high-density phone.

cards.title: Ship the Welcome sign-in screen and bound the sign-in loading state
cards.summary: A Welcome screen with one sign-in action, Create Account and account-recovery links and the legal row replaced the confusing pre-login screen, and the in-game Signing you in text now appears only for a real stored session (PR #376, building on the install gate and boot splash in PR #372). Real signed-in end-to-end testing is still outstanding.

cards.title: Fix menu accessibility: 320px clipping, 44px hit zones, Start tap recovery
cards.summary: Menu accessibility fixes: no clipping at 320px width, 44px minimum hit zones in the header, Start tap recovery and header edge padding. Merged in PR #382. The in-play pause control and the Guide header were not re-measured afterwards.

cards.title: Define one type scale and a second display typeface
cards.summary: The audit found 7 font stacks, 11 text sizes, text that shrinks to 8 px at 320 wide, and label formats that change with width. Proposal: keep Space Grotesk for body, add one squared techno display face for short uppercase labels, and set a fixed scale with a floor of 12 px for body copy. Not started beyond the font file itself.

cards.title: Ship a self-hosted Space Grotesk and wait for it before Phaser text
cards.summary: The declared brand font never actually loaded, so every device drew its own system font. PR #379 bundles Space Grotesk with the app and holds Phaser text until the font is ready, and PR #397 makes the capture harness ignore a harmless warm-reload preload hint. Merged; not yet checked on a real device.

cards.title: Add tone, scrim and motion values to the shared theme
cards.summary: Added the missing theme values the audit named (message tone colors, on-accent text, overlay scrim, motion durations) with a sync test and an off-theme color meter, with zero visual change. This only supplies the values; moving screens onto them is a separate card.

cards.title: Move scene colors onto the shared theme values
cards.summary: About 290 hard-coded color values exist in the game code and only 5 match the theme; there are 5 different near-black backgrounds, 3 greens for energy and 2 mints. The plan is to map each to a theme value or a named material extension and add a lint so new stray colors fail. Not started; large because the menu scene file is huge.

cards.title: Make the in-play pause control a 44px target
cards.summary: The pause gear is the only control during play and its hit area was 36 px in the top-right, hard to reach. The audit recommends at least 44 px with a 24 px glyph, ideally 48. Whether the menu wave also changed the play gear is unconfirmed.

cards.title: Build one shared button kit
cards.summary: There are 10 distinct button looks across 5 surfaces and no shared primary, secondary or destructive convention; START is a bare wordmark with a full-screen hit area. Proposal: 5 variants plus a toggle row and an explicit START hit zone. Not started.

cards.title: Frame the game on desktop instead of stretching the phone layout
cards.summary: At 1280x720 the menu is the phone layout stretched: tiny wordmarks and a 1100 px horizontal corridor. Proposal: a centered column or a scaled UI. Low priority because the game is phone-first.

cards.title: Define empty, loading and error states for the leaderboard
cards.summary: The empty leaderboard is a bare gray line; loading, error and username-gate states were never captured with real data. Plan: an icon, heading, one line and one action pattern. The leaderboard redesign shipped, but real-data states are unverified.

cards.title: Draw a player message surface and fix stale guest copy
cards.summary: A unified player message module exists, but auth errors, sync failures, username errors and boot errors are typed and never drawn, and six auth messages still promise guest play although guests cannot play. Plan: a bottom or top toast for the existing four tones with a fade, plus the copy fix. Not started.

cards.title: Complete the full UI rework migration on the new standards
cards.summary: UI component and layout standards are on main as registries. The full migration is under separately owned wave governance and remains open.

cards.title: Decide the six design-board picks: font, quit confirm, start style, icons, backdrop, HUD
cards.summary: Remaining graphics work (icon atlas, button kit, backdrop unification, play HUD) waits on picks for the display font, Quit-to-Menu confirmation, START style, icon construction, backdrop and play HUD. The owner first asked to walk through them one at a time, then on 2026-11-10 said to stop asking and make the judgement calls. No pick has been recorded yet.

cards.title: Ship the Chip board tile style as the default
cards.summary: The owner picked the Chip style for board tiles. The tile bake was added in the second integration and the Chip tiles, markers, wordmarks and Guide icons were wired in PR #387, with the Trace style kept as an alternate switch. Merged to main.

cards.title: Polish the Chip board: junction dots, player shape, start tile and goal alignment
cards.summary: The owner asked to remove the dots at path splits, make the player a rounded square that matches the chip tile shape, line the goal tile up exactly with its tile edges at every pixel ratio, and redesign the start tile in the same chip language. PR #402 makes all four changes and is merged and deployed to mazer.fawxzzy.com on 2026-11-10; it has not been checked on a real phone. The pad and ring on the end tiles were later removed at the owner's request (MAZER-VIS-013).

cards.title: Make the player trail iridescent with a gentle pulse
cards.summary: The owner wants the trail to look like a midnight-sun shimmer that shifts colour along its length and over time, with a gentle pulse. PR #402 adds a back-and-forth sweep through cyan, violet, orchid and apricot that avoids the player's green, the goal's red and the start's gold, clears the contrast floor against the dark underlay, and freezes to a static gradient under reduced motion. It is merged and deployed on 2026-11-10 and not yet checked on a real phone. The sweep was later made faster and a travelling sheen band added because the shift was too subtle (MAZER-VIS-013).

cards.title: Replace the edge diamonds with one new set that fires beams to and from all eight
cards.summary: The owner asked for one diamond set everywhere: sitting behind the title and menu UI, evenly spread along the screen edge with the bottom row flush to it, mirror-symmetric, and with lasers from the player out to all eight diamonds and from all eight out to the maze. The old diamond art and its image files were retired (PR #374, PR #375) and the layout and beam timeline were corrected (PR #384). Checked on test frames and the capture harness; not yet checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Make the edge diamonds orbit the screen during build and deconstruct
cards.summary: The owner wanted the eight edge diamonds to travel around the screen edge while a maze generates or deconstructs, not just spin in place. PR #388 adds one lap clockwise on build and one counter-clockwise on deconstruct, with the ring parked until the beams land. Merged and deployed; not yet checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Remove the leftover tile after deconstruct and the red square on the AI player
cards.summary: After a maze deconstructed a single tile could remain, and a red square followed the AI player when it moved. The deconstruct now switches the docks atomically (all at once or not at all) and the red marker was removed (PR #374). The lifecycle capture and analyzer found four causes of the leftover tile; two partial-strip findings are still unconfirmed.

cards.title: Restore the slower tile-by-tile maze build and deconstruct pacing
cards.summary: A timeline change made maze build and deconstruct almost instant, and the owner asked twice for the earlier pace back. PR #384 restored per-tile pacing: roughly two seconds to build level 1 and three to build level 20, with deconstruct somewhat faster than before. Whether it reads as smooth is the owner's call on a phone.

cards.title: Fix the missing maze deconstruction and fire the spawn beams after the build
cards.summary: The owner reported that the maze did not dissolve after reaching the goal and that the spawn beams fired before generation finished. Root cause was the Chip floor reveal mask treating an empty row limit as show-everything, so the full floor stayed drawn. Fixed in PR #393 with one shared reveal check; the intro now builds first, then the 8 beams fire, then the player appears. Merged and deployed; proven in a headless browser with a real key press, not yet on a real device.

cards.title: Add a goal beacon, minimum-size goal marker and legible trail on dense boards
cards.summary: On small Chip tiles the goal and trail were hard to read. PR #394 adds a goal beacon, a minimum-size goal marker and a more legible trail. Earlier goal-star work landed in PRs #321, #330 and #331. Merged to main.

cards.title: Make the player easy to find and fix readability checkpoints
cards.summary: The player was hard to find on dense boards and four palette readability checks failed on the Chip tiles with nothing asserting them. PR #399 adds a locator ring and soft glow in the player's own green with a find-me pulse on spawn, unpause and idle, and raises the model floor luminance so all 20 readability checkpoints pass. Real-phone cost and feel are not measured.

cards.title: Regenerate the HUD icons as one matched set and atlas
cards.summary: The three header icons are 1254 px AI-style PNGs in three different styles and glow treatments, shown at under 25 px, 1.5 MB in total. Plan: redraw as one outline icon family from scripted SVG, bake a single small atlas, and add the missing glyphs (close, check, info, share, install). Not started.

cards.title: Unify the backdrop across boot, install gate and sign-in
cards.summary: Three visual dialects exist: the game (black space, dot matrix), the teal-black install and sign-in pages, and the account portal. Plan: one near-black canvas color, calmer starfield on gates, the app icon on the install screen, and a dot-matrix wordmark on boot. Portal alignment is in a separate repo. Not started.

cards.title: End markers without a box, start arrow, visible trail shift, matched diamonds
cards.summary: After PR #402 went live the owner asked for five changes. (1) The square pad behind the goal star and start marker is gone: the star and play arrow sit directly on the board tile with a thin dark outline for legibility. (2) The start arrow points the way the player will first move (the first step of the solution path; down on the portrait level 1, right on landscape). (3) The trail colour shift is now clearly visible: a shorter, faster hue sweep plus a travelling white sheen band that also shifts the hue, still at least 3:1 against the chip tile and static under reduced motion. (4) The edge diamond border is always the live trail colour and (5) the colour inside the diamonds and the beams is always the player's green, both from one shared palette module. The Guide copy and icons were updated. Open as a pull request; not merged, not deployed, not checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Complete the World Identity visual maintenance lane
cards.summary: Finish bounded World Identity fixes while preserving the accepted Navigation Core, Teleport System, and gameplay contracts.

cards.title: Publish the master-backed Fawxzzy project board
cards.summary: The read-only /projects route and guarded public HTTP reader are merged source. The Mazer owner export is available; live public cards and website synchronization await the sole canonical writer's accepted sanitized projection, approved public source location, and refresh policy.

cards.title: Atlas contracts mesh
cards.summary: Define and implement Contracts v2 mesh without overstating @atlas/contracts v0.1.0 or five implemented v1 families.

cards.title: CI and delivery health
cards.summary: Recover Fitness and Playbook CI and correlate Actions with delivery without treating absence or READY as health.

cards.title: Default branch governance
cards.summary: Decide protection/ruleset posture for ten cloud repositories.

cards.title: Marker integrity
cards.summary: Keep marker names, denominators, scope, dates, receipts, and manifests coherent without rewriting history.

cards.title: Operator Surface Adoption
cards.summary: Prove four distinct operator roles without duplicate authority: Foundation portfolio, Playbook operations, Atlas Book doctrine, and _stack action routing.

cards.title: Owner metric scope alignment
cards.summary: Make owner percentages explicit by scope, date, denominator, and evidence.

cards.title: Release policy and evidence
cards.summary: Define release readiness and evidence for ten repos; zero visible releases is not readiness.

cards.title: Root truth convergence
cards.summary: Reconcile declared, generated, locked, validation, and current checkout truth without erasing timestamped provenance.

cards.title: Runtime Activation Readiness
cards.summary: Prove the accepted local runtime placement through exactly eight binary gates without inferring running uptime from stopped/restorable state or starting unadmitted persistent processes.

cards.title: Runtime Correlation Reliability
cards.summary: Prove identity, state, and receipt correlation across exactly five deterministic bounded-worker scenarios: successful, failed, duplicate, interrupted/restarted, and stale-receipt rejection.

cards.title: Source hierarchy documentation normalization
cards.summary: Normalize current-sounding docs to the accepted eight-level source hierarchy.

cards.title: Stack inventory, lock, and head reconciliation
cards.summary: Resolve four exact lock/head validation errors through canonical generation.

cards.title: Cortex boundary decision
cards.summary: Decide root-owned embedded Cortex versus remote repository authority.

cards.title: Cortex context and synthesis
cards.summary: Refresh Cortex read models, implement contract-frozen chat synthesis, and resolve the local-versus-remote boundary.

cards.title: Stale-proof refresh queue
cards.summary: Turn stale-proof classifications into a deterministic, reviewable refresh queue without granting provider or registry mutation authority.

cards.title: Direct provider read adapters
cards.summary: Add receipt-backed read-only GitHub, Vercel, and Supabase observation adapters while retaining file input as a supported fallback.

cards.title: Deterministic roadmap next command
cards.summary: Expose the stable machine roadmap through a read-only human and JSON next-work command.

cards.title: Cross-app privacy and data contracts
cards.summary: Define reusable privacy-first data boundaries for Fitness, wellness, Mazer, Trove, and future applications.

cards.title: Foundation product operating layer
cards.summary: Finish Foundation as the trusted operator dashboard for project health, data posture, deployment proof, and safe next actions.

cards.title: Foundation control-plane truth reconciliation
cards.summary: Reconcile the canonical Foundation GitHub identity and current remote evidence across config, registry, generated surfaces, fixtures, setup docs, and Atlas projection.

cards.title: Evaluate a startup backend for a measured unsupported platform
cards.summary: Add another startup installer only after a real target platform and operational need are identified.
